entity.description: A one-use pairing code an edge node's operator made (System › Edge Clients), good until expireDate (an hour by default). Only its hash is kept (codeHash, as other single-use codes). Pairing sets usedDate and the pairedNodeId it paired; a used or expired code pairs nothing.

A local node paired with this edge node, by its instance id. keyFingerprint is the SHA-256 of the public key of the client certificate it paired with (hex): a link is taken only from that key, while statusId is EdgeClientActive. linkGeneration goes up by one with each new up connection; a connection of an older generation is closed and can no longer answer or acknowledge. The versions and features are the ones its last Hello said. A pairing is one local node or one cluster of them (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.4): every member links with the key and names its own instance id, the one linkGeneration numbers all their connections, and no member is a row.

field.name: setupJson
field.description: What the node's last Configure (the Edge Node wizard's Apply, plans/archive/Edge-Node.md §5.7) set besides its host names: a JSON object of mailDomains, chatBridgeIds and passSites (the sites whose PASS authority this node is, which an mr-pass call for the site goes to), and xmppDomain and sipDomain, checked as input from any client. A site, XMPP or SIP domain another pairing named first is refused (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.1).

field.name: queueMaxMegabytes
field.description: This pairing's own size cap on the items waiting for it (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.1), in place of the conf's queue-max-megabytes, which otherwise holds for each pairing alone; the retention pass fails its oldest waiting items past it. Empty, 0 or less is unset: the conf's cap holds.

field.name: lastMemberId
field.description: The member of the pairing that linked last (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.4): every member of a local cluster links with the pairing's key and names its own instance id. With none of them linked, a node that is neither this one nor in the cluster's last member list takes the pairing over (§4.5).

field.name: holdNewMember
field.description: Y: a new node taking the pairing over is refused, held for approval, until approvedMemberId names it (§4.5). Otherwise it is admitted, logged, shown and told to the administrators.

field.name: memberKeys
field.description: Each member's own key, pinned for its instance id on its first link (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.11): a JSON array of [instanceId, SHA-256 of the key], at most 64, newest last. A member's Hello proves its key over the TLS connection; an id named with another key is a new node. forget#EdgeMember removes one.

field.name: takeoverDate
field.description: The last takeover by a new node: when, from which member (takeoverFromId) and by which (takeoverToId).

field.name: takeoverFromId
field.description: The node the last takeover displaced: refused, "taken over", until the operator clears it (clear#EdgeTakeover), so the link never goes back and forth between two copies of the data.

entity.description: A public host name this edge node answers for a paired local node (plans/archive/Edge-Node.md §5.3), lower case with no port. A name belongs to one node. In EdgeHostPassthrough mode the edge node reads the TLS ClientHello's server name and pipes the connection down the node's link, where the local node ends TLS with its own certificate; while the link is down the connection is refused. In EdgeHostTerminate mode the edge node ends TLS with its own certificate and forwards each request down the link as HTTP/2, adding the client's address; while the link is down it answers with the offline page. In EdgeHostLinkName mode (a front node, plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.7) it is an edge member's own link name, passed through to that member alone (memberId). The edge node keeps these in memory and loads them again when org.moqui.edge.EdgeServices changes one.

field.name: stickyCookie
field.description: In terminate mode, the cookie whose value picks the member of the node's pool for each request (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.4): rendezvous hashing over the live members, so a browser session stays on one member. Empty for the edge conf's sticky-cookie (moqui.session by default). No Java counterpart.

field.name: memberId
field.description: In EdgeHostLinkName mode, on a front node (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.7): the instance id of the edge member whose own link name this is. Its connections pass through untouched to that member alone, so a local node's link (its ALPN and client certificate) reaches it; while that member is not linked they are refused, never sent to another member. The front writes the row from the member's Hello. No Java counterpart.

entity.description: One unit of work queued for the other end of the link: on an edge node the items for a local node (EqdToLocal), on a local node its outbox for the edge node (EqdToEdge). pairedNodeId is the local node of the pair: on an edge node the paired node's id (decision 1), on a local node the pairing it is known by (edge_node_pairing, the same on every member of its cluster, plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.4), else its own instance id. queueItemId is a UUID, so the receiver's receipt stays unique when this database is lost and made again; sequenceNum orders the items, and the items of one conversationKey (a room, a mailbox, a phone number) are delivered one at a time in that order: a head that failed holds the ones after it until it is delivered or fails for good. idempotencyKey is unique per node and direction: enqueuing it again returns the item there is. kind names the receiver's handler service (the edge queue-kind conf). The payload is text (JSON), or contentLocation names a large body. statusEnumId: EqsPending, EqsDelivered (the receiver applied it, or had already), EqsFailed (the receiver refused it maxAttempts times, or it waited past the retention period or the size cap; kept for inspection the retention period from failedDate). A delivery holds the row (leaseOwner until leaseExpiresDate) while it waits for the answer.

view-entity.description: The head of each conversation key's items: select conversationKey and sequenceNum (the lowest), finding by pairedNodeId, directionEnumId and statusEnumId EqsPending.
The queue's items counted by the fields selected with them (pairedNodeId, directionEnumId, kind, statusEnumId): how many, the oldest queued, and their payloads' bytes.

entity.description: A queue item this node applied, from the other end of the link, by the sender's queueItemId: written in the transaction that applied it, so a redelivery (its acknowledgement was lost) finds it and is only acknowledged. pairedNodeId is the local node of the pair, as on EdgeQueueItem, so every member of a local cluster, and a standby, finds the receipts of the others. Kept for the queue's retention period.

On an edge node with the MTA in moqui (edge_mail_mta=moqui, plans/archive/Edge-Node.md §5.4 E5b), the delivery of one message a local node sent (its mailOut queueItemId) to the recipients of one domain, by that domain's MX; the domain "(local node)" is the recipients queued back to the local node itself. Written in the transaction that applies the mailOut item, so the item is delivered once these rows are there. recipientsJson is the addresses still to deliver; mailFrom the envelope sender (the VERP address when edge_mail_bounce_domain is set); contentLocation the signed message, shared by the rows of one message and removed with its last report. statusEnumId: EmdPending (nextAttemptDate is the next try), EmdSent, EmdBounced (bouncedCount refused for good, or not delivered within mail_delivery_days). sentCount and refusedText (each refused address with the answer) are what the report says; reportPending is Y while the report (the mailStatus back) is not queued yet, which each round tries again without delivering again. lastReplyText is the last answer of the MX, or why it was not reached.

On an edge node, the copy of one record of a local node's replicated set (the edge replicate conf): its entity, its primary key and the set's fields of it, as JSON, so the edge node's schema holds none of the business entities. pkHash is the SHA-256 (hex) of the canonical key JSON, by which a value is found; pkJson and fieldsJson are encrypted at rest. replicaEpoch is the local node's snapshot the value was last written under: a full resync writes every value under a new one and then removes those of older ones.

On an edge node, how far a local node's replicated set has been applied: the local node's epoch (each full resync starts one) and the sequence of the last batch applied, written in the transaction that applied it. A batch that does not follow the cursor (this database was lost, or the local node restarted) is answered with a request for a full resync. snapshotDate is when the last full resync finished.

field.name: senderToken
field.description: When the local node's member that sent the last batch took the sender lock (epoch milliseconds): a batch with an earlier one is refused, as it comes from a member that lost the lock (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.4).

entity.description: On an all-in-one node (node_role=all-in-one, plans/archive/Edge-Node.md §10), a record of a paired node's replicated set that was not applied because it claims an item the server holds itself: a mail address, a chat bridge id or a phone number (claimKind: MailAddress, ChatBridge, PhoneNumber; itemKey the item). The server's own item wins; ownerText names its holder. Keyed as the EdgeReplicaValue it would have been, with the record kept (pkJson and fieldsJson, encrypted at rest, as the value's) so it is applied once the server no longer holds the item (recheck#ReplicaConflicts, and each later batch of the set). A later batch that deletes the record, or a full send that no longer has it, removes the row. firstDate is when it was first refused, lastDate when last.

On an edge node, a file of a message its local node sends by address (an MMS picture), put here with the send (the queue kind chatMedia), so the network fetches it from the edge node at /channels/{chatBridgeId}/media/{token} (plans/archive/Edge-Node.md §5.4, E6). edgeMediaId is the SHA-256 (hex) of the token, which the local node makes and only it and the network know; location is the file, under dbresource://moqui/edge/media/. Served until expireDate (channels_media_minutes after it came), then removed with its file.

On an edge node, a TCP port whose connections each go down one paired local node's link as a byte tunnel (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.1, §4.10 Ports, E16): tunnelKind ssh to the node's SSH server, xmpp (STARTTLS) or xmpps (direct TLS) to its XMPP server, which ends the TLS, and on a front node (node_role front, §4.7) smtp to the SMTP listener of a member of the pairing's pool (an edge cluster's mail edge), with a PROXY v2 header naming the client. A port is one row; the node listens on it while its pairing is active, within seconds of org.moqui.edge.EdgeServices adding it (on edge_ssh_tunnel_host, edge_xmpp_host or edge_smtp_tunnel_host, every address when empty) and stops when it is removed. The conf's own tunnel ports are apart: edge_ssh_tunnel_port goes to the one active pairing, and edge_xmpp_port and edge_xmpp_tls_port to the node whose XMPP domain a client names.

On a local node whose cluster members each link to the edge node (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.4, "Work from the pool to the edge node"), the member that sends replication and keeps the link's own rows (CallMediaNode, SipNode) and the phone numbers' fallbacks: lockName replicate. On a node that takes links (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.6), the member of an edge cluster whose SIP engine registers the trunks: lockName sipTrunks. A member claims it and renews the lease (the database's time) while it holds it; a lease that lapsed is taken over by another member, which then sends each replicated set whole, or registers the trunks. A member that stops lets it go. No Java counterpart.

On a node that takes links, in an edge cluster (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.6): the local members each edge member holds links of, by pairing (linksJson, an object of pairing to member ids), one row per edge member. It is written as a link is admitted (in the transaction that locks the pairing's row), and every few seconds while another member of the edge cluster is live (heartbeatDate, the database's time); removed when the member stops, and pruned after a day. Admission on any edge member counts a local member linked on another one, whose row is fresh, as linked (plans/Edge-Node2.md §4.11), so a node that holds only the pairing's key is refused while a real member is linked anywhere, and a member's link to a second edge member is not a takeover. No Java counterpart.
